title: Perhaps
text:
As I was intent only on my chimera,

I did not notice what was around me; one day

fertile spring surprised me,

smiling over all the broad field.


Green leaves were budding

from the swollen buds of the branches,

and yellow, white, red flowers

cheered the blotch of the landscape.


And it was a rain of golden arrows,

the sun over the youthful fronds;

in the broad river's sonorous current

the graceful poplars gazed at themselves.


After so much road, it is the first

time I have watched spring break forth,

I said, and afterward, declaimingly:


"How late now for my happiness!"

And then, as I walked, like one who feels

wings of another illusion: "And still

I shall reach my youth one day!"
editorial_note: The translation keeps Machado's turn from belated spring recognition to the renewed illusion of youth.

title: Last Night When I Was Sleeping...
text:
Last night when I was sleeping

I dreamed, blessed illusion!,

that a fountain flowed

inside my heart.


Tell me, by what hidden channel,

water, do you come to me,

spring of new life

from which I never drank?


Last night when I was sleeping

I dreamed, blessed illusion!,

that I had a beehive

inside my heart;


and the golden bees

were making there,

with old bitterness,

white wax and sweet honey.


Last night when I was sleeping

I dreamed, blessed illusion!,

that a burning sun was shining

inside my heart.


It was burning because it gave

warmths of a red hearth,

and it was sun because it lit

and because it brought tears.


Last night when I was sleeping

I dreamed, blessed illusion!,

that what I had

inside my heart was God.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the recurring dream refrain and the heart's movement from water to hive, sun, and God.

title: Evil
text:
While the red spittle of grapeshot

whistles, furrowing the blue sky, day after day,

and, scarlet or green, near the laughing king

battalions sink, set aflame in masses;


while an unbridled madness crushes

and turns a thousand men into smoking loam;

poor dead! sunk in summer, in the grass,

in your joy, Nature, who created them holy,


there is a God who laughs among the damasks

of the altar, at incense, at chalices of gold,

who, rocked by Hosannas, sweetly falls asleep.


But he starts awake when mothers yoked

to anguish and weeping beneath their black caps

offer him a farthing wrapped in their handkerchief.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the antiwar contrast between slaughtered soldiers, ritual luxury, and grieving mothers.

title: Evening Prayer
text:
Like an angel seated in a barber's hands,

I live, raising the deeply ribbed tankard,

hypogastrium and neck bowed, with my pipe,

under a swollen wind of light veils.


Like warm droppings from old dovecotes,

a thousand Dreams give me gentle burnings


and my sad heart resembles the sapwood

bloodied by the ocher golds the tree weeps.


Then, after carefully swallowing my Dreams,

I turn and, after drinking thirty or forty tankards,

I collect myself, releasing my fierce urgencies:


meek as the Lord of cedar and hyssop,

I piss toward the brown sky, high, high, so far...

with the consent of the heliotropes.
editorial_note: The translation preserves Rimbaud's grotesque parody of prayer, mixing sacred diction with bodily irreverence.

title: At the Green Cabaret
text:
At five in the evening


I had already spent eight days with my boots split

because of the pebbles; and I arrived at Charleroi.

At the Green Cabaret I ordered slices of toast

with butter and juicy, warming ham.


I stretched both legs out, happy, under the green

table, while I looked at the naive drawings

of the wallpaper. What joy when the little maid,

the one with big breasts and eyes like embers


—she, yes, is not frightened by a simple kiss—,

laughing, offered me toast with butter

and warm ham, on a many-colored plate!


White and pink ham perfuming a clove

of garlic; and she filled my enormous mug: foam

that gilded the glow of an almost sleeping sun.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the hungry traveler's tavern relief, earthy sensuality, and late-afternoon glow.
